meta.homeTitle: Avo: Android apps and games on your Mac
meta.homeDescription: Use Android apps and play Android games on your Mac, each in its own window. Free and open source, for Macs with Apple chips.
meta.ogAlt: The Avo app icon on a dark green background.

release.downloadMeta: Free, for Macs with Apple chips
release.unreleasedNote: Only preview builds for testers so far. Follow Avo on GitHub to hear when it's ready.

hero.title: Android apps and games, right on your Mac.
hero.lede: Each app opens in its own window, like any Mac app. Play games with your keyboard, mouse or controller.
hero.shotAlt: Avo's library window on a Mac: a game to pick up where you left off, then rows of Android games and apps.

games.title: Play with keyboard, mouse or controller.
games.lede: Turn on Game Mode, and your keys and mouse work like fingers on the screen.
games.keysTitle: Put keys where you need them
games.keysText: Drag keys onto the game's buttons. Ready-made layouts for shooters, MOBAs and racing games get you started.
games.aimText: In shooters, move the mouse to look around, just like on a PC.
games.padText: Connect a game controller to your Mac and play.
games.shareText: Save your key layout and share it with other players.
games.fairText: Avo adds no auto-aim or other advantages to games. Some online games may still refuse to run in Avo.
games.shotPlayText: The mouse aims, each key presses the button under it, and the frame rate shows in the corner.
games.shotPlayAlt: A shooter in its own Mac window, with round labels for W, A, S, D, Q, E, Space and the mouse buttons placed over the game's touch controls, and the frame rate in the top corner. Player names are blurred.
games.shotKeysText: Add a key, drag it onto a button, then press the key you want to use. Templates get you started.
games.shotKeysAlt: Avo's key editor over a game's lobby: a toolbar with Add Control and Templates, and key labels such as W, A, S, D, Q, E and the mouse buttons placed on the game's buttons.
games.shotNote: Player names and account numbers in these screenshots are blurred.

mac.title: Every Android app works like a Mac app.
mac.windowsTitle: Its own window and Dock icon
mac.windowsText: Find apps in Launchpad and Spotlight, and switch between them with ⌘Tab.
mac.notifText: App alerts show up in Notification Center.
mac.clipText: Copy on your Mac, paste in Android, or the other way around. Links open in your Mac's browser.
mac.followText: Dark mode, time zone and language follow your Mac's settings.
mac.translateText: Press <kbd>⌘</kbd><kbd>⇧</kbd><kbd>T</kbd> to translate the text in any app.
mac.captureText: Capture just the app, nothing else on your screen.
mac.alsoText: Trackpad gestures, drag and drop, sound and location work too.
mac.notYet: Camera and Bluetooth don't work yet.
mac.artDockAlt: A Dock with separate icons for several Android apps.

tour.title: Set it up your way.
tour.lede: A look around Avo's settings, as they look today.
tour.graphicsText: Android draws on your Mac's graphics chip. Cap games at 30, 60, 90 or 120 frames per second or match your display, and choose how sharp and how large things look.
tour.graphicsAlt: Avo's Graphics settings: the renderer is set to Automatic and uses the Mac's graphics chip, the frame rate cap is 60, and there are controls for render scale, interface size, scaling filter and sharpness.
tour.privacyText: Choose which phone model apps see, and whether Android can use your Mac's location.
tour.privacyAlt: Privacy & Security settings: a device profile set to identify as a OnePlus 13, with its chipset, graphics and screen listed, and a switch that shares the Mac's location with Android.
tour.fingerprintsText: Apps that ask for a fingerprint still work. Name a finger, then click Touch when an app asks for it.
tour.fingerprintsAlt: Fingerprints settings: a finger named Right thumb with a Touch button, a field to add another finger, and an option to touch with an unregistered finger.
tour.androidText: See which version of Android you have, change to another, or go back to the one before. Reset Android for a fresh start.
tour.androidAlt: Android settings: Android 17 is installed with the June 2026 security update, Android 16 is kept as the previous version, and there are buttons to change versions, switch back or reset Android.
tour.googleText: Google Play isn't included, but you can add it. Avo shows what's installed and helps you register with Google before you sign in.
tour.googleAlt: Google Apps settings: the Play Store and Play services are installed, the Android ID is blurred, and a button copies the ID to register with Google before signing in.
tour.generalText: Send app alerts to Notification Center, and put Android apps on your Desktop or in the Dock.
tour.generalAlt: General settings: app alerts show in Notification Center, with switches for app aliases on the Desktop and apps in the Dock, and a button to recreate shortcuts.

how.title: A small Android, running quietly on your Mac.
how.step1Text: Avo keeps a small Android system running out of sight. You never see a phone screen.
how.step2Text: When you open an app, it appears in its own Mac window.
how.step3Text: Apple chips run Android apps directly, without slow translation.

req.title: What you need
req.macTitle: A Mac with an Apple chip
req.macText: M1 or newer. Intel Macs aren't supported.
req.osText: Avo needs features that arrived in macOS 15.
req.gpuText: Install Google's free Android Emulator from Android Studio. Avo uses it to draw games on your graphics chip.

dev.title: Open source, with the tools you know.
dev.adb: Connect adb and Android Studio with one switch in Settings.
dev.root: Test on Android 17, with a root shell and a command-line tool.
dev.source: All the code is on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license. Build it yourself or send a pull request.

built.textNamed: Made by {maintainer} in West Kalimantan, with help from Claude.
built.textAnon: Made by an independent developer in West Kalimantan, with help from Claude.

support.title: Avo is free. Your support keeps it going.
support.text: Avo is built and maintained by one independent developer. Your support goes straight to that work: development tools, test hardware, and the Apple Developer Program fee that lets Avo open without a security warning.
support.note: Support goes to the developer personally. It is not a purchase and does not come with features or priority help.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.a1: Yes. No price, no ads and no account needed.
faq.a2: Preview builds for testers are on GitHub Releases. Avo is still in early development, so expect rough edges.
faq.a3: We're still testing. Some online games block programs like Avo, and Avo won't try to get around that.
faq.a4: It isn't included, but you can add it in Avo's settings. Other stores, like F-Droid, work too.
faq.a5: Usually not. Most banking apps only run on a real phone.
faq.a6: Android runs walled off from the rest of your Mac, and Avo's code is open for anyone to check.
faq.q7: Does it work on Intel Macs?
faq.a7: No. You need a Mac with an Apple chip, M1 or newer.
faq.a8: To the developer, personally. It pays for the tools and hardware Avo is built and tested with, and for the Apple Developer Program fee that lets Avo open without a security warning.
